objective: Under G18, at the coordinator's pick with the owner's intuition that time is a fold: in ordinary growth with no added rule, is there a quantity on the path of reading (orders of births between two ends that agree, or readings of one end's descent) that is well defined, two-valued and multiplicative, and does it put a sign across a split so that two ways of reaching one configuration cancel? Stop at such a quantity with a frozen test, or at an argument that every path quantity of the recorded laws is trivial.
status: Complete 2026-11-26 (obstruction learned by argument; referee pending): on the orders of one history every sign is +1 around each square unless a chosen attribute or the exchange rule tells two births apart; on the readings of one end the sign is a chosen character that reduces to the exchange sign along growth; and nothing in the law sums over orders: the missing piece is a sum over histories. A renaming census kept, not run.
title: Time as a fold: is there a sign on the path of reading?
